lit-cl-01-c4.text: Milman Parry (1930). Studies in the Epic Technique of Oral Verse-Making: I. Homer and Homeric Style. Harvard Studies in Classical Philology 41 (hosted by the Center for Hellenic Studies, Harvard).
lit-cl-01-c4.quote: Parry defines the formula as "a group of words which is regularly employed under the same metrical conditions to express a given essential idea" (p. 80).
lit-cl-01-c4.claim: Performers used formulaic phrases ('rosy-fingered dawn,' 'wine-dark sea,' 'swift-footed Achilles') that fit specific metrical positions.
